module_name: Information Diffusion and Virality: Cascades, Epidemic Models, Trending Prediction
module_description: Module 17 models how content spreads: cascade trees, classical epidemic models (SIS/SIR on networks), branching process and Hawkes/temporal point process models for bursts, influence versus homophily as competing explanations, and prediction of what will trend. It connects to platform design (recommender amplification) so students can separate organic spread from algorithmic distribution.
learning_outcomes: C3 Reconstruct cascades and compute structural virality
C4 Fit a simple diffusion model and predict spread
C5 Discuss recommender amplification as a confound
methods_models: Cascade reconstruction, IC/LT simulation, Hawkes fitting, survival analysis of cascade size
Feature-based trending classifiers (early features -> later spread)
evaluation_metrics: Precision@k for trending prediction, cascade-size distribution fit, log-loss/ranking metrics, structural virality vs size correlation
pitfalls_limitations: Sampling only surviving cascades, platform-side ranking effects misread as content quality, early engagement not being causal, deleted-content survivorship
tools_stack: networkx, numpy/scipy, tick (Hawkes), lifelines, tweepy/Bluesky clients; R: igraph + survival packages
lab_activities: Reconstruct cascades for a topic, compare with an SIR fit, build a trending predictor from early features
datasets_apis: Public cascade data (X/Bluesky topic cascades, imitation dataset)
assessment_methods: Lab notebook plus graph figures and a short interpretation; graded on correctness of metrics and defensibility of substantive claims
data_collection_workflow: Build the interaction graph from collected data -> deduplicate accounts and edges -> compute metrics -> cluster communities -> archive graph object and code
textbooks: Zafarani et al., Social Media Mining, ch. on diffusion
Barabasi, Network Science, ch. on epidemic spreading
Goel et al. (2016) 'The structural virality of online diffusion'
key_papers: 2024-2026 papers on prediction of virality and on recommender-driven spread
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: algorithm-driven feeds (TikTok For You) made pure 'organic virality' modelling harder; analysis now separates creator-side from platform-side amplification
industry_relevance: Used in disinformation/trust-and-safety teams, political-communication research units, community-management analytics, and influence-marketing measurement; network metrics are standard deliverables in crisis-mapping briefings.
localization_context: Practised on Indonesian case networks (election-issue discussion, anti-hoax communities, local brand mentions) where the platform mix and language mix differ from US/EU benchmark datasets.
ethics_regulation: Re-identification risk of pseudonymous accounts, doxxing risk when publishing ego-networks, and the ethical line between mapping influence and surveilling individuals; UU PDP applies to any data tied to identifiable accounts.
case_study_scenarios: Explain and predict which policy posts will spread widely on X next week.
deliverable_format: Cascade dataset + diffusion model + prediction demo
